$comment: STOS command database, written from the STOS User Guide (Mandarin/Jawx 1988) and the reference card in own words. Format: docs/commands.md.

commands.name: auto
doc: Direct command: the editor types the next line number for you each time you press Return. Without values it starts at 10 and counts in steps of 10.

commands.name: change
doc: Replaces every a$ in the program by b$. Give a line range to limit where it changes.

commands.name: clear
doc: Wipes all variables and the banks made by the program, and sets the READ pointer back to the first DATA line.

commands.name: cont
doc: Carries on with a program that was stopped by STOP or Control+C, at the next instruction. Only works if the program was not edited in between.

commands.name: default
doc: Puts the editor back to its start-up state and redraws its windows. Unlike RESET it can also be used inside a program.
Not the same as DEFAULT PHYSIC / LOGIC / BACK (screen addresses).

commands.name: delete
doc: Removes program lines. Forms like `DELETE 100`, `DELETE 100-200`, `DELETE -200` and `DELETE 100-` work as for LIST.

commands.name: english
doc: Switches the editor messages and command names to English (the default). See FRANCAIS.

commands.name: francais
doc: Switches the editor to French. ENGLISH switches back.

commands.name: language
doc: Tells which language (English or French) the editor is set to.
commands.unclear: Only on the reference card; no entry found in the manual OCR. Page 40 is the ENGLISH/FRANCAIS entry. Check the return values.

commands.name: fload
doc: Opens the file selector and loads the program you pick. path$ is the search pattern shown in the selector.

commands.name: follow
doc: Tracing for debugging: shows each line as it runs, optionally only between two lines, and can print chosen variables as they change. FOLLOW OFF stops it.

commands.name: free
doc: Gives the number of bytes still free for your program. It also tidies the string memory, which can take a moment.

commands.name: frequency
doc: Toggles the screen refresh between 50 and 60 Hz, for monitors that can show 60 Hz.

commands.name: fsave
doc: Saves the current program under a name chosen in the file selector.

commands.name: full
doc: Makes the current editor window fill the whole screen; other programs are not affected.

commands.name: grab
doc: Copies program number n (or only lines first to last of it) into the current program, so separately tested parts can be joined.

commands.name: keylist
doc: Lists what text is assigned to each function key. Shifted keys appear as 11 to 20.

commands.name: list
doc: Shows the program, or a range of it, on screen.

commands.name: lower
doc: Back to the normal listing style: commands in lower case, variables in upper case. See UPPER.

commands.name: merge
doc: Adds a program from disc to the one in memory. Lines with the same number are replaced by the loaded ones.

commands.name: multi
doc: Splits the editor into n windows, one per program segment, so several programs can be seen at once.

commands.name: new
doc: Erases the current program from memory. Other program segments stay. UNNEW may bring it back.

commands.name: renum
doc: Renumbers the program (or lines start to end) beginning at number, in steps of inc (both 10 when left out). GOTO and GOSUB targets are updated.

commands.name: reset
doc: Restarts the editor and redraws the screen.

commands.name: run
doc: Starts the current program from its first line, from a given line, or loads a program from disc and runs it.

commands.name: search
doc: Finds the text s$ in the program and shows the line. SEARCH alone goes to the next match.

commands.name: system
doc: Leaves STOS and goes back to the GEM desktop. Anything not saved is lost.

commands.name: unnew
doc: Tries to restore a program erased by NEW. Only works if nothing new was typed in between.

commands.name: upper
doc: Listing style with commands in upper case and variables in lower case. LOWER switches back.

commands.name: hexa
doc: Chooses whether LISTBANK shows its numbers in hexadecimal (ON) or decimal (OFF).

commands.name: dim
doc: Creates an array. Several arrays and several dimensions are allowed; each dimension can hold up to 65535 elements and starts at element 0.

commands.name: inc
doc: Adds 1 to an integer variable. Same result as var=var+1, but faster.

commands.name: dec
doc: Takes 1 from an integer variable. Same result as var=var-1, but faster.

commands.name: let
doc: Assigns a value to a variable. The word LET is optional.

commands.name: left$
doc: As a function: the first n characters of a string. On the left of `=` it replaces the first characters of v$ instead.

commands.name: right$
doc: As a function: the last n characters of a string. On the left of `=` it replaces the last characters of v$.

commands.name: mid$
doc: As a function: n characters of v$ starting at character s (the first character is 1). On the left of `=` it overwrites that part of v$.

commands.name: instr
doc: Looks for str2$ inside str1$, from character p if given. Returns the position where it was found, or 0.

commands.name: sort
doc: Sorts a whole array (strings, integers or reals) into ascending order. Always give element 0.

commands.name: match
doc: Searches a sorted array for value and returns its element number. When it is missing, a negative number points to the closest entry.
commands.unclear: The OCR of the not-found result is unclear; check page 49.

commands.name: lower$
doc: Returns the string in small letters.

commands.name: space$
doc: A string made of n spaces.

commands.name: string$
doc: A string of n copies of the first character of a$.

commands.name: chr$
doc: The character with Ascii code n.

commands.name: asc
doc: The Ascii code of the first character of a$.

commands.name: len
doc: The number of characters in a$, invisible ones included.

commands.name: val
doc: Turns the number written in a string into a value; 0 if there is no number.

commands.name: str$
doc: Turns a number into a string.

commands.name: hex$
doc: The number as a hexadecimal string starting with $, optionally with n digits.

commands.name: bin$
doc: The number as a binary string starting with %, optionally with n digits.

commands.name: listbank
doc: Shows the banks in use with their number, type, address and size.

commands.name: reserve as screen
doc: Reserves a temporary bank big enough for a whole screen. Temporary banks are not saved with the program.

commands.name: reserve as datascreen
doc: Reserves a permanent bank for a screen; it is saved with the program.

commands.name: reserve as work
doc: Reserves a temporary work area of length bytes (rounded up to 256). Banks 1 to 4 are best left to the system.

commands.name: reserve as data
doc: Reserves a permanent bank of length bytes that is saved with the program.

commands.name: reserve as set
doc: Reserves a permanent bank for a character set (font). See CHARCOPY and CHARLEN.

commands.name: bcopy
doc: Copies a whole bank to another bank number (1 to 15).

commands.name: bgrab
doc: Copies all banks, or only bank b, from another program segment into the current program.

commands.name: erase
doc: Deletes bank b and frees its memory.

commands.name: start
doc: The address in memory where bank b begins, of the current program or of program prgno.

commands.name: length
doc: The size of bank b in bytes; 0 means the bank does not exist.

commands.name: save
doc: Saves according to the extension: .BAS a program, .ASC the listing as text, .MBK one bank (give its number), .MBS all banks, .VAR the variables, .PI1/.PI2/.PI3 or .NEO a screen, .PRG a program that runs from the desktop.

commands.name: load
doc: Loads according to the extension: a program, banks, variables or a picture. Pictures and banks can be loaded into a given bank or screen (for example `,back`).

commands.name: bsave
doc: Saves the memory from start to end to a file as raw bytes.

commands.name: bload
doc: Loads a file unchanged into memory at an address or into a bank.

commands.name: accload
doc: Loads an accessory (.ACB) so it can be called from the Help menu. `ACCLOAD "*"` loads every accessory on the disc.

commands.name: accnew
doc: Removes all loaded accessories from memory.

commands.name: accnb
doc: Inside a program: 0 when it runs normally, or its program number (4 to 15) when it runs as an accessory.
if accnb then print "Running as an accessory"

commands.name: sprite
doc: Shows sprite n (1 to 15) at screen position x,y with image p from the sprite bank (bank 1). The position is that of the image's hot spot.

commands.name: move x
doc: Gives sprite n a list of horizontal moves. Each move is `(speed,step,count)`: wait speed/50 s between steps, move step pixels (negative = left), count times (0 = forever). `L` at the end loops the list; `E` followed by a position stops the sprite there. Start it with MOVE ON.

commands.name: move y
doc: Like MOVE X, but vertical: a positive step moves the sprite down.

commands.name: move
doc: MOVE ON starts the moves set by MOVE X / MOVE Y, MOVE OFF stops them, MOVE FREEZE pauses them (MOVE ON continues). Without n all sprites are affected.

commands.name: movon
doc: Not zero while sprite n is still moving, 0 when it stands still.

commands.name: x sprite
doc: The x position of sprite n.

commands.name: y sprite
doc: The y position of sprite n.

commands.name: limit sprite
doc: Sprites are only drawn inside this rectangle; parts outside are cut off. Their positions are not limited. Without values the whole screen is used again.

commands.name: anim
doc: Animates sprite n through a list of images. Each step is `(image,delay)` with the delay in 50ths of a second; `L` loops. ANIM ON starts, ANIM OFF stops, ANIM FREEZE pauses; without n all sprites.

commands.name: collide
doc: Tests whether other sprites touch a box of w by h pixels around the hot spot of sprite n (0 = mouse). The result has one bit per sprite that touches it (bit 1 = sprite 1, ...); 0 means no collision.

commands.name: set zone
doc: Defines rectangle number z on the screen, to be tested later with ZONE.

commands.name: zone
doc: The number of the first zone (made with SET ZONE) that sprite n is in, or 0. Sprite 0 is the mouse pointer.
if zone(0)=1 then print "Mouse in zone 1"

commands.name: reset zone
doc: Removes zone z, or all zones.

commands.name: detect
doc: The colour of the background pixel under the hot spot of sprite n (0 = mouse), useful to test collisions with the scenery.
if detect(1)=4 then print "On the water"

commands.name: put sprite
doc: Stamps a copy of sprite n onto the screen as part of the background. The sprite itself is not changed. Use WAIT VBL after it.

commands.name: get sprite
doc: Grabs the screen area at x,y into existing image i of the sprite bank (same size as that image). The hot spot is set to x,y. The mask is the colour treated as transparent (0 when left out). The area must be fully on screen.

commands.name: priority
doc: Sprite order on screen. OFF (normal): lower sprite numbers appear in front. ON: sprites lower on the screen (larger y) appear in front, which gives a sense of depth.

commands.name: autoback
doc: Normally graphics are drawn both on the screen and on the hidden background screen used by sprites. AUTOBACK OFF draws only on the screen: much faster, but moving sprites will wipe the drawing away.

commands.name: update
doc: UPDATE OFF stops sprites being redrawn automatically (they still move, but invisibly); UPDATE redraws the changed sprites once; UPDATE ON goes back to normal.

commands.name: redraw
doc: Redraws all sprites at their current positions, changed or not.

commands.name: off
doc: Stops all sprite moves and animations and removes the sprites from the screen. Function key f10 does this in the editor.

commands.name: freeze
doc: Pauses all sprite moves, animations and music. UNFREEZE carries on.

commands.name: unfreeze
doc: Continues sprite movements and music paused by FREEZE.

commands.name: change mouse
doc: Changes the mouse pointer: 1 arrow (default), 2 pointing hand, 3 clock. Higher numbers use an image from the sprite bank.
commands.unclear: How m maps to a sprite image number is cut off in the OCR; check page 96.

commands.name: x mouse
doc: The x position of the mouse pointer (also when it is hidden).

commands.name: y mouse
doc: The y position of the mouse pointer (also when it is hidden).

commands.name: mouse key
doc: Which mouse buttons are held: 0 none, 1 left, 2 right, 3 both.
if mouse key=1 then print "Left button"
commands.unclear: The value table is garbled in the OCR; check page 97.

commands.name: limit mouse
doc: Keeps the mouse pointer inside a rectangle. Without values the whole screen is allowed again.

commands.name: hide
doc: Makes the mouse pointer invisible; X MOUSE and Y MOUSE still work. Each HIDE must be matched by a SHOW before the pointer comes back. HIDE ON hides it regardless of that count.

commands.name: show
doc: Shows the mouse pointer again; it needs as many SHOWs as there were HIDEs. SHOW ON shows it regardless of the count.

commands.name: joy
doc: Reads the joystick as a number with one bit per direction (up, down, left, right) and one for the fire button.
commands.unclear: The bit numbers are missing in the OCR (example uses `joy and 15` for the four directions); check page 99.

commands.name: jleft
doc: True (-1) while the joystick is pushed left, else false (0).

commands.name: jright
doc: True (-1) while the joystick is pushed right.

commands.name: jup
doc: True (-1) while the joystick is pushed up.

commands.name: jdown
doc: True (-1) while the joystick is pulled down.

commands.name: fire
doc: True (-1) while the fire button is pressed.

commands.name: play
doc: Plays one note. pitch goes from 1 (low) to 96 (high) in semitones, 12 per octave; 0 just waits. duration is in 50ths of a second. voice is 1 to 3; without it all three voices play. The program waits until the note ends.

commands.name: volume
doc: Sets the loudness from 0 (silent) to 15 (loud) for voice v, or all voices. 16 hands the volume to the envelope set with ENVEL.

commands.name: click
doc: Turns the key click on or off. Switch it off when playing sounds, as key presses would cut them off.

commands.name: music
doc: MUSIC n plays tune n (1 to 32) from the music bank (bank 3, made with the music accessory) in the background while the program goes on. MUSIC OFF stops it, MUSIC FREEZE pauses it, MUSIC ON starts again (from the pause after FREEZE).

commands.name: tempo
doc: Speed of the music played by MUSIC, from 1 (very slow) to 100 (very fast).

commands.name: transpose
doc: Shifts the music played by MUSIC by df semitones (-90 to +90); negative is lower.

commands.name: pvoice
doc: Where the music on voice v has got to (the address of the note being played); 0 when that voice plays nothing.

commands.name: voice
doc: Mutes (OFF) or unmutes (ON) voice v of the music, or all three voices.

commands.name: boom
doc: Explosion sound. Turn off the key click and freeze any music first for a clean result.

commands.name: noise
doc: Plays a hiss, like wind, on voice v or all voices. p goes from 1 (high) to 31 (low). It keeps sounding while the program runs; shape it with ENVEL.

commands.name: envel
doc: Applies one of the sound chip's envelope shapes (type 1 to 15) to sounds from PLAY and NOISE; speed sets how long one cycle lasts (larger is slower). Set VOLUME 16 first.

commands.name: psg
doc: Reads or writes register r of the ST's sound chip directly, for effects the other sound commands cannot make.
commands.unclear: Described in the appendix on the sound chip; check the register list on page 271.

commands.name: cls
doc: Clears the whole screen, or a given screen (PHYSIC, BACK, LOGIC or a screen bank), optionally with colour col and only inside a rectangle.

commands.name: ink
doc: Colour (palette index) used by the drawing commands that follow.

commands.name: colour
doc: Sets palette entry index to a colour from 512, written as $RGB with each part 0 to 7.

commands.name: colour
doc: The $RGB value now assigned to palette entry index.

commands.name: palette
doc: Sets several palette entries at once, from entry 0 onward.

commands.name: plot
doc: Sets one pixel to the ink colour, or to colour index.

commands.name: point
doc: The colour index of the pixel at x,y.

commands.name: draw
doc: Draws a line between two points, or from the last point drawn to a new one.

commands.name: box
doc: Draws an outlined rectangle between two corners.

commands.name: polyline
syntax: POLYLINE x1,y1 TO x2,y2 TO x3,y3 ...
doc: Draws connected lines through all the points in one go.

commands.name: arc
doc: Draws part of a circle around x1,y1 with radius r, between two angles given in tenths of a degree (0 to 3600).

commands.name: earc
doc: Like ARC, but part of an ellipse with horizontal radius r1 and vertical radius r2.

commands.name: set line
doc: Line style: mask is a 16-bit pattern (1 = drawn, 0 = gap), thickness 1 to 40, and each end can be 0 square, 1 arrow or 2 round.

commands.name: paint
doc: Flood-fills the closed shape around x1,y1 with the ink colour and the fill style from SET PAINT.

commands.name: rbar
doc: Draws a filled rectangle with rounded corners.

commands.name: polygon
syntax: POLYGON x1,y1 TO x2,y2 TO x3,y3 ...

commands.name: circle
doc: Draws a filled circle around x1,y1 with radius r, using INK and SET PAINT.

commands.name: pie
doc: A filled slice of a circle (a filled ARC), for pie charts.

commands.name: ellipse
doc: Draws a filled ellipse with horizontal radius r1 and vertical radius r2.

commands.name: epie
doc: A filled slice of an ellipse.

commands.name: set paint
doc: Fill style for filled shapes: type 0 none, 1 solid, 2 dotted (pattern 1 to 24), 3 lined (pattern 1 to 12), 4 your own pattern from SET PATTERN. border chooses whether an outline is drawn.

commands.name: set pattern
doc: Installs your own fill pattern (16 by 16), used when SET PAINT type is 4: from an address (a bank, or VARPTR of a variable) or straight from a string, for example one taken with SCREEN$.

commands.name: flash
doc: Makes palette entry index cycle through a list of $RGB colours, each shown for delay 50ths of a second, in the background. FLASH OFF stops all flashing (entry 2 flashes by default).

commands.name: shift
doc: Rotates the palette colours every delay 50ths of a second, from entry start (default 1) upward, for waterfall-style effects. SHIFT OFF stops it.
commands.unclear: SHIFT OFF is not in the OCR syntax line; check page 139.

commands.name: gr writing
doc: How drawing combines with what is already there: 1 replace (default), 2 transparent, 3 XOR, 4 inverse transparent. Not the same as WRITING for text.

commands.name: polymark
doc: Draws a marker (chosen with SET MARK) at each point.

commands.name: set mark
doc: Marker for POLYMARK: 1 point, 2 plus, 3 star, 4 square, 5 diagonal cross, 6 diamond. size is the width in pixels, in eight steps from 6 to 83 (6, 17, 28, ...); the point has only one size.

commands.name: mode
doc: Switches a colour monitor between low resolution (0, 16 colours) and medium resolution (1, 4 colours).

commands.name: mode
doc: The current resolution: 0 low, 1 medium, 2 high (monochrome).

commands.name: divx
doc: Divide x coordinates by this to draw on a pretend 640 by 400 screen in any resolution: 2 in low resolution, 1 in medium and high.

commands.name: divy
doc: Divide y coordinates by this: 2 in low and medium resolution, 1 in high. See DIVX.

commands.name: clip
doc: Restricts all drawing to a rectangle; CLIP OFF removes the limit.

commands.name: back
doc: Address of the background screen that sprites restore behind them. Can be used wherever a screen is expected (CLS, LOAD, SCREEN COPY ...).

commands.name: physic
doc: Address of the screen being shown. Setting it shows another screen at once.

commands.name: logic
doc: Address of the screen that text and graphics commands draw on; normally the same as PHYSIC. Drawing on a hidden logical screen and then using SCREEN SWAP gives flicker-free graphics.

commands.name: screen swap
doc: Exchanges the physical and logical screens, so the picture just drawn becomes visible. The swap takes effect at the next vertical blank (use WAIT VBL).

commands.name: default physic
doc: The address the physical screen had when STOS started.

commands.name: default logic
doc: The address the logical screen had when STOS started.

commands.name: default back
doc: The address the background screen had when STOS started.

commands.name: get palette
doc: Sets the colours to those stored with the screen in bank n (or at a screen address).

commands.name: zoom
doc: Copies a rectangle of screen scr1 into a (usually larger) rectangle, stretching it. The target is the logical screen unless scr2 is given.

commands.name: reduce
doc: Shrinks the whole of screen scr1 into the rectangle x1,y1 to x2,y2; the opposite of ZOOM.

commands.name: screen copy
doc: Copies a whole screen, or a rectangle of it, very fast to another screen. x coordinates are rounded down to a multiple of 16.

commands.name: screen$
doc: Stores a rectangle of a screen in a string, and puts such a string back at x,y. Good for moving blocks of graphics around.

commands.name: def scroll
doc: Defines scrolling zone n (1 to 16): the rectangle and how far (dx, dy pixels) it moves each time SCROLL n is used. Not the window SCROLL UP / DOWN.

commands.name: scroll
doc: SCROLL n moves zone n as set by DEF SCROLL. SCROLL OFF / ON switch off or on the automatic scrolling of the current text window when the cursor passes the bottom (page 174).

commands.name: wait vbl
doc: Waits for the next vertical blank (the start of a new screen picture, 50 times a second). Keeps animation smooth and lets screen changes take effect.

commands.name: synchro
doc: SYNCHRO OFF stops the automatic sprite moves every 50th of a second; SYNCHRO then performs one step of all moves, so they can be kept in step with scrolling. SYNCHRO ON goes back to normal.

commands.name: unpack
doc: Unpacks a screen compressed with the screen compactor accessory (or PACK) from bank bnk onto screen scr.

commands.name: pack
doc: Compresses screen scr into bank bnk and returns the packed length.
commands.unclear: The syntax line reads `I=PACK scr,bnk` while the example uses `pack(5,6)`; check page 160.

commands.name: appear
doc: Fades the picture at address or bank x onto the screen with a special effect y (1 to 79).

commands.name: fade
doc: Gradually changes the palette in the background: to black, to the colours of the screen in bank sbank, or to a list of new colours. speed is the number of 50ths of a second between steps.

commands.name: inverse
doc: Swaps the text and background colours for the text that follows.

commands.name: shade
doc: Prints the text that follows dimmed.

commands.name: writing
doc: How text combines with what is under it: 1 replace (default), 2 OR, 3 XOR. For graphics see GR WRITING.
commands.unclear: The card says OR is the default, the manual says replacement; check page 165.

commands.name: locate
doc: Puts the text cursor at column x, row y of the current window.

commands.name: xtext
doc: Converts a graphic x coordinate into a text column.

commands.name: ytext
doc: Converts a graphic y coordinate into a text row.

commands.name: xgraphic
doc: Converts a text column into a graphic x coordinate.

commands.name: ygraphic
doc: Converts a text row into a graphic y coordinate.

commands.name: square
doc: Draws a box wx characters wide and hy high at the text cursor, with border style border (1 to 16).

commands.name: home
doc: Moves the text cursor to the top left of the current window.

commands.name: cdown
doc: Moves the text cursor down one line.

commands.name: cup
doc: Moves the text cursor up one line.

commands.name: cleft
doc: Moves the text cursor one place left.

commands.name: cright
doc: Moves the text cursor one place right.

commands.name: xcurs
doc: The column of the text cursor.

commands.name: ycurs
doc: The row of the text cursor.

commands.name: set curs
doc: Sets the height of the text cursor: its top and bottom line inside the character (1 to 8 in low and medium resolution).

commands.name: curs
doc: Shows or hides the flashing text cursor.

commands.name: centre
doc: Prints a$ centred on the cursor's line.

commands.name: tab
doc: Used in PRINT: moves the cursor n places to the right.

commands.name: scrn
doc: The Ascii code of the character shown at text position x,y.

commands.name: windopen
doc: Opens text window n at column x1, row y1, w characters wide and h high, with an optional border style (1 to 16) and character set. It becomes the current window.

commands.name: title
doc: Writes a title into the top border of the current window.

commands.name: border
doc: Changes the border style of the current window (1 to 16).

commands.name: window
doc: Makes window n the current window and brings it to the front.

commands.name: qwindow
doc: Like WINDOW, but faster, because the window is not redrawn.

commands.name: windon
doc: The number of the current window.

commands.name: windmove
doc: Moves the current window with its contents to text position x1,y1.

commands.name: windel
doc: Closes window n and restores what was under it.

commands.name: clw
doc: Clears the current window with its paper colour.

commands.name: scroll up
doc: Scrolls the current window up one line.

commands.name: scroll down
doc: Scrolls the text from the cursor line down one line.

commands.name: charlen
doc: The length of the character set in bank n; 0 if there is none.

commands.name: charcopy
doc: Copies character set s into bank b, for example to edit it or use it in a window.

commands.name: icon$
doc: A string that prints icon n (from the icon bank) at the cursor. It can also be used as a menu title or option.

commands.name: menu$
doc: Builds the menu bar: menu title x, and option y under title x, with optional colours. OFF greys out (disables) an option, ON enables it again. Start the menu with MENU ON.

commands.name: menu on
doc: Shows the menu bar made with MENU$. border is the frame style (1 to 16); mode 1 gives drop-down menus, 2 pull-down menus.

commands.name: menu off
doc: Removes the menu completely and frees its memory.

commands.name: menu freeze
doc: Stops the menu from reacting until MENU ON.

commands.name: mnbar
doc: The number of the menu title chosen, 0 if none.
if mnbar=1 and mnselect=1 then end

commands.name: mnselect
doc: The number of the option chosen in the menu.

commands.name: on menu
doc: Jumps to a line depending on the menu title chosen (line1 for title 1, ...), checked automatically while the program runs once ON MENU ON is given. ON MENU OFF stops it.
on menu goto 1000,2000 : on menu on

commands.name: goto
doc: Jumps to a line. The line number may be calculated, e.g. `goto 100*N`.

commands.name: gosub
doc: Calls the subroutine at a line; RETURN comes back to the instruction after the GOSUB.

commands.name: return
doc: Ends a subroutine and goes back to just after the GOSUB that called it.

commands.name: pop
doc: Forgets the return address of the current GOSUB, so you can leave a subroutine with GOTO instead of RETURN.

commands.name: for
doc: Starts a loop: var counts from start to finish (by inc, default 1) and the lines up to NEXT are repeated for each value.
for I=1 to 10 : print I : next I

commands.name: to
doc: Part of FOR (the end value) and of many commands that take a range or two points (DRAW, BOX, BAR, SCREEN COPY, CHANGE ...). A reserved word: no variable name may contain it.

commands.name: step
syntax: FOR var=start TO finish STEP inc
doc: Sets how much the FOR variable changes each time round; may be negative.
for I=10 to 0 step -2 : print I : next I

commands.name: next
doc: Ends a FOR loop: adds the step and goes round again until the end value is passed.
for I=1 to 3 : print I : next I

commands.name: while
doc: Repeats the lines up to WEND as long as the condition is true. The test is done at the start, so the loop may run zero times.

commands.name: repeat
doc: Starts a loop that runs until the condition after UNTIL is true. The test is at the end, so it runs at least once.

commands.name: until
doc: Ends a REPEAT loop; goes back to REPEAT while the condition is false.

commands.name: if
doc: Runs statements1 when the condition is true, otherwise statements2. After THEN or ELSE a line number alone means GOTO that line. Everything stays on one line.
if A>10 then print "Big" else print "Small"

commands.name: then
doc: Part of IF: what follows is done when the condition is true.

commands.name: else
syntax: IF condition THEN statements1 ELSE statements2
doc: Part of IF: what follows is done when the condition is false.
if A=1 then print "One" else print "Other"

commands.name: stop
doc: Stops the program and returns to the editor; CONT carries on.

commands.name: on
doc: Jumps to (or calls) the first line when var is 1, the second when it is 2, and so on. Other values go on to the next instruction.

commands.name: on error
doc: When an error happens, jump to line instead of stopping. ERRN and ERRL tell which error and where; finish with RESUME. ON ERROR GOTO 0 switches this off.

commands.name: resume
doc: Leaves an error routine: retry the instruction that failed, carry on after it (NEXT), or go to a line. Do not leave an error routine with GOTO.

commands.name: errn
doc: The number of the last error (list in Appendix A).

commands.name: errl
doc: The line where the last error happened.

commands.name: error
doc: Causes error number n on purpose, as if it really happened. Useful to hand an error you do not deal with back to STOS.

commands.name: break
doc: Allows (ON) or blocks (OFF) stopping the program with Control+C.

commands.name: key
doc: Gives function key x (1 to 10, shifted 11 to 20) a text of up to 64 characters that it types when pressed.

commands.name: inkey$
doc: The key waiting in the keyboard buffer, or "" if none; it does not wait. Keys without a character (function and cursor keys) give chr$(0); see SCANCODE.

commands.name: scancode
doc: The scan code of the last key read by INKEY$, to tell keys apart that have no Ascii code.
K$=inkey$ : if K$<>"" then print scancode

commands.name: input$
doc: Reads exactly n characters from the keyboard (waiting for each, nothing shown), or count characters from a file or device.

commands.name: fkey
doc: The function key pressed: 1 to 10, 11 to 20 with Shift, 0 if none.

commands.name: wait key
doc: Waits until a key is pressed.

commands.name: key speed
doc: Sets the key repeat: the time between repeats and the delay before repeating starts, in 50ths of a second.

commands.name: put key
doc: Puts text into the keyboard buffer as if it were typed; for example to leave a command for the editor when the program ends.

commands.name: input
doc: Asks for values from the keyboard (or reads them from a file or device) and stores them in the variables. Several values are typed separated by commas.

commands.name: line input
doc: Like INPUT, but each value is ended by Return (or by separator$ for files), so commas are kept as part of the text.

commands.name: print
doc: Writes values on the screen (or to a file or device). `;` keeps the cursor after the value, `,` moves to the next column. `?` is a short form.

commands.name: using
doc: Formatted output in PRINT. In the format string `#` stands for a digit, `.` for the decimal point, `+` always shows the sign, `-` only a minus, `^` gives exponent form, and `~` is replaced by the next character of a string. Other characters are printed as they are.
commands.unclear: The OCR mixes up some format characters (`~`, `;`); check pages 202-203.

commands.name: open out
doc: Opens a file for writing with PRINT #, on channel 1 to 10. An existing file of that name is erased.

commands.name: open in
doc: Opens a file for reading with INPUT #.

commands.name: open
doc: Opens a random access file (records, see FIELD), or a channel to the serial port, MIDI port or printer.

commands.name: close
doc: Closes a file; changes are only safe on disc after closing.

commands.name: eof
doc: True when the end of the file has been reached.

commands.name: lof
doc: The length of an open file.

commands.name: pof
doc: The current read/write position in an open file; assign to it to move the position.

commands.name: field
doc: Defines the layout of one record of a random access file: each field is a string of fixed length.

commands.name: as
doc: Part of FIELD and RESERVE. A reserved word: no variable name may contain it.

commands.name: put
doc: Writes the field strings as record number r of a random access file.

commands.name: get
doc: Reads record number r of a random access file into the field strings.

commands.name: port
doc: True when a device (serial, MIDI) has data waiting to be read.

commands.name: lprint
doc: Like PRINT, but to the printer.

commands.name: llist
doc: Lists the program, or part of it, on the printer (same forms as LIST).

commands.name: ldir
doc: Prints the disc directory on the printer.

commands.name: hardcopy
doc: Prints a picture of the screen (like Alt+Help).

commands.name: windcopy
doc: Prints the text of the current window; much faster than HARDCOPY.

commands.name: dir
doc: Lists the files of the current directory, or those matching path$. DIR/W lists them across the screen.

commands.name: dir$
doc: The current directory used for loading and saving; assign to it to change directory.

commands.name: dir first$
doc: The name and details of the first file matching path$, or "" if none. flag chooses the kinds of file, one bit each: 0 normal, 1 read-only, 2 hidden, 3 system, 4 disc name, 5 folders, 6 archived; -1 means all.

commands.name: dir next$
doc: The next file matching the pattern given to DIR FIRST$, or "" when there are no more.

commands.name: previous
doc: Moves the current directory up one level.

commands.name: drive
doc: The current drive number: 0 is A, 1 is B, and so on.

commands.name: drive$
doc: The current drive as a letter.

commands.name: drvmap
doc: The connected drives, one bit per drive starting with bit 0 for A.
if btst(2,drvmap) then print "Drive C present"

commands.name: dfree
doc: Free bytes on the current disc.

commands.name: kill
doc: Deletes a file. Wildcards (`*`, `?`) delete several, so take care.

commands.name: rename
doc: Gives a file a new name.

commands.name: fileselect$
doc: Shows the STOS file selector with pattern path$, an optional title and border style (1 to 16). Returns the chosen file name, or "" if cancelled.

commands.name: sin
doc: The sine of an angle in radians.

commands.name: cos
doc: The cosine of an angle in radians.

commands.name: tan
doc: The tangent of an angle in radians.

commands.name: asin
doc: The angle (in radians) whose sine is number (-1 to 1).

commands.name: acos
doc: The angle (in radians) whose cosine is number (-1 to 1).

commands.name: atan
doc: The angle (in radians) whose tangent is number.

commands.name: pi
doc: The number pi (3.14159...), half a turn in radians.

commands.name: exp
doc: e raised to the power y#; the opposite of LN.

commands.name: int
doc: Rounds down to a whole number.

commands.name: sgn
doc: The sign: -1 if negative, 0 if zero, 1 if positive.

commands.name: max
doc: The larger of two values (numbers, or strings of the same type).

commands.name: swap
doc: Exchanges the contents of two variables of the same type.
commands.unclear: The syntax line reads `SWAP(X,Y)` but every example uses `swap A,B`; check page 220.

commands.name: def fn
doc: Defines your own one-line function, used later with FN.

commands.name: fn
doc: Calls a function made with DEF FN.

commands.name: rnd
doc: A random whole number from 0 to y. A negative y gives the last value again.

commands.name: fix
doc: How real numbers are printed: 0 to 15 gives n decimals, 16 or more gives as many as needed without trailing zeros, negative gives exponent form with ABS(n) decimals.

commands.name: time$
doc: The clock time as "HH:MM:SS"; assign to it to set the clock.

commands.name: date$
doc: The date as "DD/MM/YYYY"; assign to it to set the date.

commands.name: rol
doc: Rotates the bits of a variable n places to the left; bits leaving at the top come back at the bottom. .B, .W, .L work on 8, 16 or 32 bits.

commands.name: ror
doc: Rotates the bits of a variable n places to the right.

commands.name: btst
doc: True if bit number bit (0 to 31) of the variable is 1.

commands.name: bset
doc: Sets a bit of a variable to 1.
commands.unclear: The syntax lines say `BSET(x,y)` with x the variable, but the examples put the bit number first; check page 227 (also BCHG, BCLR).

commands.name: bchg
doc: Flips a bit of a variable (1 becomes 0 and 0 becomes 1).

commands.name: bclr
doc: Sets a bit of a variable to 0.

commands.name: peek
doc: The byte (0 to 255) at an address.

commands.name: poke
doc: Writes a byte to an address.

commands.name: deek
doc: The two-byte word at an even address.

commands.name: doke
doc: Writes a two-byte word (0 to 65535) to an even address.

commands.name: leek
doc: The four-byte long word at an even address.

commands.name: loke
doc: Writes a four-byte long word to an even address.

commands.name: varptr
doc: The address where a variable's value is kept in memory.

commands.name: copy
doc: Copies a block of memory (even addresses).

commands.name: fill
doc: Fills a block of memory with a four-byte value.

commands.name: hunt
doc: Searches memory between two addresses for a string; returns its address, or 0.

commands.name: call
doc: Runs machine code at an address or in a bank (give the bank number). Registers can be passed with AREG and DREG.

commands.name: areg
doc: Six pseudo-variables holding address registers A0 to A5, passed to and from CALL and TRAP.

commands.name: dreg
doc: Pseudo-variables holding data registers D0 to D7, passed to and from CALL and TRAP.

commands.name: trap
doc: Calls 68000 trap n (0, 1, 13, 14 for the operating system, 3 to 7 for STOS) after putting the parameters on the stack. Parameters are words unless written `L.value` (long); a string passes its address. Registers can also be passed with AREG and DREG. Mistakes easily crash the ST.

commands.name: wait
doc: Pauses for x 50ths of a second.

commands.name: timer
doc: A counter that goes up by one every 50th of a second; can be set.
timer=0 : wait key : print timer/50;" seconds"

commands.name: rem
doc: A comment: the rest of the line is ignored.

commands.name: data
doc: Values stored in the program, read with READ.

commands.name: read
doc: Reads the next values from DATA lines into variables.

commands.name: restore
doc: Makes the next READ start at the DATA of the given line.

commands.name: not
doc: Logical NOT: flips every bit, so NOT TRUE is FALSE.
Power: x raised to y. Highest priority of the operators.
Subtraction. With strings it removes every b$ from a$.

commands.name: and
doc: Logical (bitwise) AND; in IF it means both conditions.
if X>0 and X<320 then plot X,100

commands.name: or
doc: Logical (bitwise) OR; in IF it means at least one condition.
if K$="q" or K$="Q" then end
Equal to (in a comparison), or assignment. Strings are compared by their Ascii codes.
Less than; strings are compared by Ascii code.
